Reliability Across Facets: Repeats and Occasions

Source: R/reli_facet_test.R
reli_facet_test.Rd

The name of this function is experimental and may change (it was briefly gstudy_test() during development); its arguments may change too.

Estimates one reliability coefficient or one standard error of measurement (SEM) when each subject is measured more than once by each item (rater, device): for example 3 operators each scanning 20 participants twice. The extra measurements separate error within a rater from disagreement between raters, which icc_test() and reli_err_test() cannot do with one measurement per subject and item. The measurements can be exchangeable repeats within each subject-by-item cell (the default), or shared occasions (occasion: every rater measured every subject on day 1 and again on day 2). The model is the generalizability-theory (G-study) model for that design. Returns an object of class "htest" with a confidence interval and an optional test.

Usage

reli_facet_test(
  x = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  measure = NULL,
  item = NULL,
  id = NULL,
  occasion = NULL,
  stat = c("ICC", "SEM"),
  facet = c("intra", "inter", "overall"),
  type = c("consistency", "agreement"),
  k_avg = 1,
  m_avg = 1,
  r_avg = 1,
  scale = c("raw", "log", "mean"),
  method = c("anova", "reml"),
  conf.level = 0.95,
  null.value = NULL,
  alternative = c("two.sided", "greater", "less"),
  ci_method = c("auto", "mls", "satterthwaite"),
  boot = FALSE,
  boot_ci = c("auto", "perc", "bca", "stud", "basic"),
  replicates = 1999,
  se_method = c("jackknife", "normal")
)

Arguments

x

A formula of the form values ~ item | id, with several rows per subject and item. Leave NULL to use measure, item and id. Wide data are not supported.

data

A data frame containing the variables.

measure, item, id

Column names (character) of the measurement, the item (trial, rater, or occasion) and the subject identifier, for data in long format.

occasion

NULL (default) when the measurements within each subject-by-item cell are exchangeable repeats, or the name of the column identifying shared occasions (e.g. day 1 and day 2, the same for every item). See "Nested or crossed".

stat

"ICC" (default), a reliability coefficient, or "SEM", the standard error of measurement. See Details.

facet

Which measurement varies: "intra" (default), the same item on another repeat or occasion (intra-rater, repeatability); "inter", another item (on the same occasion, with occasion); or "overall", another item on another occasion (the same as "inter" without occasion). See Details.

type

"consistency" (default) sets systematic differences between items (and occasions) aside, to be reported separately; "agreement" counts them as error, as in icc_test(). Without occasion, facet = "intra" has no systematic effects and type makes no difference.

k_avg, m_avg, r_avg

The planned score (D-study): the mean of k_avg items, m_avg occasions and r_avg repeats (defaults 1, a single measurement). k_avg must be 1 for facet = "intra" and m_avg must be 1 for facet = "inter" and without occasion; r_avg must be 1 for crossed data with one measurement per subject, item and occasion.

scale

For stat = "SEM", the scale it is reported on: "raw" (default), "log" (sympercents) or "mean" (percentage of the grand mean), as in reli_err_test(). Must be "raw" for stat = "ICC".

method

"anova" (default) for balanced data (every subject measured by every item, on every occasion, the same number of times), or "reml" (a linear mixed model) for missing cells or unequal numbers of repeats.

conf.level

Confidence level of the interval (default 0.95).

null.value

A value to test against, on the scale of the estimate. The default, NULL, gives the estimate and interval without a test.

alternative

"two.sided" (default), "greater" or "less". For an SEM, "less" tests whether the error is below an acceptable value. Used only when null.value is given.

ci_method

The analytic interval when it is not exact: "auto" (default), "mls" (modified large-sample) or "satterthwaite". See Details. Ignored when the interval is exact or boot = TRUE.

boot

If TRUE, use a nonparametric bootstrap that resamples subjects for the interval and p-value. Default FALSE.

boot_ci

Bootstrap interval type: "auto" (default), "perc", "bca", "stud" (studentized) or "basic". With method = "anova", "auto" uses "bca" for an agreement SEM that counts systematic differences between items or occasions and "stud" otherwise ("perc" when se_method = "normal"); with method = "reml" it uses "perc". See Details. Used only when boot = TRUE.

replicates

Number of bootstrap replicates (default 1999).

se_method

How the standard error on the working scale is estimated: "jackknife" (default; delete one subject at a time) or "normal" (normal theory, delta method). Reported in stderr and used by the studentized bootstrap.

Value

A list of class c("reli_htest", "htest") containing:

statistic, parameter

The F (coefficients) or \(\chi^2\) (SEM) statistic and its df, when a test was requested with an exact or Satterthwaite method (z for SEMs with scale = "mean").

p.value

The p-value, when a test was requested.

conf.int

The confidence interval.

estimate

The estimate.

stderr

Standard errors of the estimate and on the working scale (z: \(-\log(1 - \rho)/2\) for coefficients, the log for SEMs), from se_method; with boot = TRUE, also boot.

null.value, alternative, method, data.name

As for an htest.

components

The variance components with intervals and shares.

nested

With occasion and facet = "intra": the estimate the repeat model (occasions ignored) would give.

fit

The mean squares, degrees of freedom and fitted model.

data

The data in long format.

settings

The settings used, for the methods.

boot

Bootstrap details (NULL unless boot = TRUE).

Details

Nested or crossed. Ask whether "measurement 2" is the same event for every item. If each operator simply scanned each participant twice, in no shared order, the measurements are exchangeable repeats nested in the subject-by-item cell: leave occasion = NULL. If every operator measured everyone on day 1 and again on day 2, the days are shared occasions: give occasion. Treating occasions as repeats counts day-to-day shifts as repeat error, so the intra-rater error looks larger and cannot be split into a systematic shift (fixable) and noise. With occasion, the result (in nested) and summary() also give what the repeat model would have estimated.

Model. All effects are random. Without occasion, with n subjects, k items and r repeats per cell, $$y_{pir} = \mu + p + i + (pi) + e_{pir};$$ with occasion (m occasions), $$y_{pio} = \mu + p + i + o + (pi) + (po) + (io) + (pio, e),$$ where with one measurement per subject, item and occasion the three-way interaction and the error are not separable (the residual). Further repeats within each subject, item and occasion are allowed and add a separate repeat error. The ANOVA estimators are unconstrained: a negative variance component estimate is kept (as icc_test() keeps a negative ICC), so a coefficient can be negative. The component table in components (and summary()) shows each component with an interval and its share of the variance of a single measurement. The model is the unrestricted (random facets) one used by lme4 and by McGraw and Wong (1996); for the consistency forms the items may be regarded as fixed, which changes the interpretation but not the computation.

Estimands. Following Brennan (2001), the facet that stays the same is part of the subject's score, and the facets that vary are error. For a planned score that is the mean of \(k'\) items (k_avg), \(m'\) occasions (m_avg) and \(r'\) repeats (r_avg), the error variance (SEM\(^2\)) is:

facetScoreConsistency errorAgreement adds
intra, repeats\(\sigma^2_p + \sigma^2_{pi}\)\(\sigma^2_e/r'\)(nothing)
intra, occasions\(\sigma^2_p + \sigma^2_{pi}\)\((\sigma^2_{po} + \sigma^2_{pio,e})/m'\)\((\sigma^2_o + \sigma^2_{io})/m'\)
inter, repeats\(\sigma^2_p\)\(\sigma^2_{pi}/k' + \sigma^2_e/(k'r')\)\(\sigma^2_i/k'\)
inter, occasions\(\sigma^2_p + \sigma^2_{po}\)\((\sigma^2_{pi} + \sigma^2_{pio,e})/k'\)\((\sigma^2_i + \sigma^2_{io})/k'\)
overall, occasions\(\sigma^2_p\)\(\sigma^2_{pi}/k' + \sigma^2_{po}/m' + \sigma^2_{pio,e}/(k'm')\)\(\sigma^2_i/k' + \sigma^2_o/m' + \sigma^2_{io}/(k'm')\)

(with further repeats within subject, item and occasion, the residual is split and its error part is also divided by \(r'\)). The coefficient (stat = "ICC") is score / (score + error). The intra-rater coefficient is the correlation between two measurements by the same item, pooled over items (it assumes the same error for every item; check() shows the within-cell SD by item). With occasions, the inter-rater coefficient is for raters on the same occasion, what most inter-rater studies report; "overall" is for any rater on any occasion, and its coefficients are the generalizability (\(E\rho^2\)) and dependability (\(\Phi\)) coefficients of G theory. In gauge R&R terms (repeats), \(\sigma^2_e\) is repeatability and \(\sigma^2_i + \sigma^2_{pi}\) reproducibility.

What averaging does. Without occasion and with \(r' = r\) (the score averages as many repeats as the study had), the inter-rater consistency coefficient is the consistency ICC of the cell means, \((F - 1)/(F - 1 + k/k')\) with \(F = MS_P/MS_{PI}\), identical to icc_test() on the cell means; it is not the reliability of a single measurement unless r = 1. Averaging the repeats before calling icc_test() is therefore only right when the scores used in practice are also means of r repeats.

Intervals and tests. An estimand that is a multiple of one mean square (an SEM) or a function of the ratio of two (a coefficient) has an exact interval and test: without occasion, the intra SEM (\(\chi^2\) on \(MS_W\)) and the inter-rater consistency SEM and coefficient with \(r' = r\). The others are approximate:

  • "mls": modified large-sample intervals for linear combinations of mean squares (Graybill & Wang, 1980; Ting et al., 1990; Burdick & Graybill, 1992). For a coefficient \(\rho\), the interval holds the values \(\rho_0\) for which the MLS interval of \(\sigma^2_{score} - \rho_0 \sigma^2_{total}\) contains 0. The p-value inverts the interval, so there is no test statistic.

  • "satterthwaite": the SEM uses a \(\chi^2\) distribution with Satterthwaite df; a coefficient uses an F test of \(\sigma^2_{score} - \rho_0 \sigma^2_{total} = 0\), the positive and negative parts each with Satterthwaite df (McGraw & Wong's device for ICC(A,1)), and the interval inverts it.

  • "auto" uses MLS, chosen in simulations (see "Simulations").

SEMs with scale = "mean" use a Wald interval on the log scale with a delta-method SE that includes the uncertainty of the grand mean.

Bootstrap. boot = TRUE resamples subjects, each with all its measurements, as in icc_test(). Resampling subjects keeps the same items and occasions, so for statistics that count systematic differences between them as error, the mean squares of the effects without subjects (items, occasions, items by occasions) are also multiplied by independent \(\chi^2_{df}/df\) draws (the hybrid step). The p-value inverts the interval and is approximate.

Unbalanced data. method = "reml" fits the model with lme4 and keeps the analytic inference, with degrees of freedom from the observed data and the harmonic mean number of repeats in place of r, and gives a warning.

Simulations. Repeats (no occasion): with 10 or 30 subjects, 2, 3 or 5 items, 2 or 3 repeats, four mixes of variance components and normal data (2000 data sets per setting), the exact intervals covered 0.940 to 0.951 and the MLS intervals at least 0.939 for every estimand (0.95 to 0.96 on average; slightly conservative for \(\Phi\)), hence ci_method = "auto" uses MLS. The Satterthwaite intervals were similar for the intra-rater and consistency statistics but fell to 0.67 to 0.74 for the agreement SEM and coefficient with 2 items when systematic differences between items were the main error. With REML and unbalanced data (30 subjects, 20% of repeats missing, or 1 to 3 repeats per cell), the MLS intervals covered 0.937 to 0.969.

Occasions (2 or 3 items, 2 or 3 occasions, one measurement per cell, four mixes including a large day effect and large rater bias, 2000 data sets per setting): the MLS intervals covered at least 0.934 with 30 subjects and 0.928 with 10, for every facet, type and statistic; the Satterthwaite intervals fell to 0.69 to 0.79 for the agreement statistics.

Uneven tails for agreement statistics. The agreement statistics include a component estimated from very few degrees of freedom (items, or occasions: k - 1 or m - 1). The MLS bound that this component drives is wide, and the other bound is close to nominal. With 30 subjects and 95% two-sided intervals, the agreement coefficients fell below their lower limit 0 to 1% of the time and above their upper limit about 3% (nominal 2.5% each; two-sided coverage up to 0.97 to 0.99 with occasions), and the agreement SEMs fell above their upper limit 0 to 0.6% of the time and below their lower limit 3 to 6%. So the usual one-sided tests are conservative: a coefficient greater than a threshold (alternative = "greater") and an SEM less than an acceptable error (alternative = "less"). The opposite one-sided tests can be somewhat liberal (up to about 6% instead of 2.5% for an agreement SEM greater than a threshold). With REML and 20% of cells missing, MLS covered 0.922 to 0.979. Treating the occasions as exchangeable repeats (leaving out occasion) gave intra-rater SEM intervals that covered the true agreement SEM only 0.24 to 0.92 of the time (0.04 to 0.87 for the consistency SEM, which it overstated by 30% on average).

With skewed, heavy-tailed data every analytic interval under-covered (0.78 to 0.90 with repeats). The studentized bootstrap was then the best interval for every statistic except the agreement SEM, for which BCa was best, hence boot_ci = "auto": with repeats it covered 0.90 to 0.93 for the intra-rater and consistency statistics with 30 subjects (2 or 3 items, 2 repeats, 300 data sets of 499 replicates per setting). As in reli_err_test(), agreement statistics with few items (or occasions) and large systematic differences between them under-covered with every method (0.69 to 0.85 with 2 or 3 items); more items help more than more subjects. Resampling subjects without the hybrid step covered as little as 0.15 there. With normal data the analytic intervals were better than any bootstrap interval. With occasions (2 days), the bootstrap gave the same "auto" choices and helped for the consistency statistics (0.92 to 0.93 with skewed data), but for the agreement statistics the MLS interval was as good or better even with skewed data, and every interval under-covered when a day effect on 2 days dominated the error.

Other software. VCA (variance components for deeper nesting and laboratory precision designs), rptR (repeatability for non-Gaussian data), gtheoryr (crossed multi-facet G-studies and D-study design optimisation), SixSigma (ss.rr(), gauge R&R summaries) and MethComp (method comparison with linked replicates and method-specific variances) fit related models. This function adds intervals and tests for the coefficients and the intra- and inter-rater SEMs, and the link to mdc_test().

References

Brennan, R. L. (2001). Generalizability Theory. Springer. doi:10.1007/978-1-4757-3456-0

Burdick, R. K., & Graybill, F. A. (1992). Confidence Intervals on Variance Components. Marcel Dekker.

Graybill, F. A., & Wang, C. M. (1980). Confidence intervals on nonnegative linear combinations of variances. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 75(372), 869-873. doi:10.1080/01621459.1980.10477565

McGraw, K. O., & Wong, S. P. (1996). Forming inferences about some intraclass correlation coefficients. Psychological Methods, 1(1), 30-46. doi:10.1037/1082-989X.1.1.30

Ting, N., Burdick, R. K., Graybill, F. A., Jeyaratnam, S., & Lu, T.-F. C. (1990). Confidence intervals on linear combinations of variance components that are unrestricted in sign. Journal of Statistical Computation and Simulation, 35(3-4), 135-143. doi:10.1080/00949659008811240

See also

icc_test() and reli_err_test() for one measurement per subject and item; mdc_test(); reli_htest-methods for summary(), plot() and check().

Examples

# 12 participants, 3 operators, 2 scans each (exchangeable repeats)
set.seed(2)
scans <- expand.grid(scan = 1:2, operator = c("A", "B", "C"), id = 1:12)
subj <- rnorm(12, 50, 5)
bias <- c(A = 0, B = 1.5, C = -1)
scans$thickness <- subj[scans$id] + bias[scans$operator] +
  rnorm(nrow(scans), 0, 1.5)

# Intra-rater (repeatability) ICC and SEM
reli_facet_test(thickness ~ operator | id, data = scans)
#> 
#> 	Intra-rater ICC (same item, another repeat), for a single measurement
#> 	with MLS interval
#> 
#> data:  thickness ~ operator | id
#> 
#> alternative hypothesis: two.sided
#> 95 percent confidence interval:
#>  0.7084019 0.9523049
#> sample estimates:
#> ICC(intra) 
#>  0.8627703 
#> 
reli_facet_test(thickness ~ operator | id, data = scans, stat = "SEM")
#> 
#> 	Intra-rater SEM (same item, another repeat), for a single measurement
#> 	with exact interval
#> 
#> data:  thickness ~ operator | id
#> 
#> alternative hypothesis: two.sided
#> 95 percent confidence interval:
#>  1.467683 2.344365
#> sample estimates:
#> SEM(intra) 
#>   1.804801 
#> 

# Inter-rater agreement for a single scan by any operator
res <- reli_facet_test(thickness ~ operator | id, data = scans,
                       facet = "inter", type = "agreement")
summary(res)
#> The estimated ICC(inter,A) was 0.827 (95% compatibility interval
#> [0.227, 0.937]). Values in this interval are the most compatible with
#> the data, given the model and its assumptions. The estimate is the
#> inter-rater ICC (absolute agreement, another item), for a single
#> measurement, with error from: items, subjects x items, repeats (within
#> cells). The data had 12 subjects, 3 items (72 measurements, 2
#> measurements per subject-by-item cell); variance components were
#> estimated by analysis of variance (unconstrained). The interval is a
#> modified large-sample (MLS) interval for a ratio of linear combinations
#> of mean squares (Graybill & Wang, 1980; Ting et al., 1990).
#> 
#> Variance components:
#>  Component              Variance 95% CI        SD   Percent
#>  subjects               21.0     [10.3, 61.2]  4.58 81.1   
#>  items                  1.63     [0.368, 68.1] 1.28 6.3    
#>  subjects x items       -0.512   [0, 0.716]    0    0.0    
#>  repeats (within cells) 3.26     [2.15, 5.50]  1.80 12.6   

# D-study: the mean of 2 scans by one operator
reli_facet_test(thickness ~ operator | id, data = scans, facet = "inter",
                type = "agreement", r_avg = 2)
#> 
#> 	Inter-rater ICC (absolute agreement, another item), for the mean of 2
#> 	repeats with MLS interval
#> 
#> data:  thickness ~ operator | id
#> 
#> alternative hypothesis: two.sided
#> 95 percent confidence interval:
#>  0.2320697 0.9641056
#> sample estimates:
#> ICC(inter,A) 
#>    0.8841374 
#> 

# If scan 1 and scan 2 were shared days, the same for every operator
day1 <- reli_facet_test(thickness ~ operator | id, data = scans,
                        occasion = "scan", type = "agreement")
day1
#> 
#> 	Intra-rater ICC (absolute agreement, same item, another occasion), for
#> 	a single measurement with MLS interval
#> 
#> data:  thickness ~ operator | id, occasions: scan
#> 
#> alternative hypothesis: two.sided
#> 95 percent confidence interval:
#>  0.2672571 0.9511654
#> sample estimates:
#> ICC(intra,A) 
#>    0.8624128 
#> 
day1$nested
#> $estimate
#> ICC(intra) 
#>  0.8627703 
#> 
#> $components
#>                component   variance      lower      upper       sd   percent
#> 1               subjects 20.9911484 10.3465885 61.2025740 4.581610 81.100437
#> 2                  items  1.6344496  0.3684636 68.1309585 1.278456  6.314784
#> 3       subjects x items -0.5122982  0.0000000  0.7155093 0.000000  0.000000
#> 4 repeats (within cells)  3.2573063  2.1540936  5.4960478 1.804801 12.584779
#> 

# Smallest difference between two operators beyond measurement error
mdc_test(reli_facet_test(thickness ~ operator | id, data = scans,
                         stat = "SEM", facet = "inter",
                         type = "agreement"))

#> 	Minimal detectable change (95%, two-sided) from the inter-rater SEM
